text: The pipeline is built, scheduled, validated, and connected to Power BI. This lesson is about the part none of that preparation is actually for: the meeting where you hand the answer back to the Store Operations lead.

The report page should mirror exactly what matters. One KPI card at the top, large: yesterday's total sales amount, the one number this whole project exists to deliver. Below it, a short trend chart of the last couple weeks, giving that number context without needing a second meeting to explain it. And the order count from Gold as a smaller secondary figure, answering the natural next question before anyone has to ask it.

In the room, open with the answer, not the build. Yesterday's total sales were this number, combining both in-store and online. Only if asked, explain how — one sentence: this refreshes automatically every morning from a pipeline that cleans and combines both channels' data, so you're never looking at something stale or manually pulled.

Two questions will come up. Can you trust this number — and the honest answer is specific, not reassuring: every morning, the pipeline checks that cleaned data never has more rows than the raw data it came from, and that the daily summary has exactly as many rows as there are real days of sales, automatically, before the number ever reaches this report. And can you break it out by store — say so plainly: that's a real, useful follow-up, just not in this version, which only answers the daily total. That's new scope, not a failure.
That's how you present what you built. Last lesson, you'll recap the whole pipeline and see exactly where it's headed next.
